messages:
SRE-Bot: :rotating_light: Incident detected: PrivateLink connection for customer ACME degraded in eu-west-3 (AZ-b). RTT spikes + intermittent DNS failures observed by health checks. Pager sent to #oncall.

Mira K.: seeing the alert. Confirming: which paths are impacted? whole peering or specific AZ?

Jon P.: initial telemetry shows DNS responses from the PrivateLink endpoint in AZ-b are returning NXDOMAIN intermittently. Other AZs (a,c) look OK. BGP sessions stable.

Priya S.: ACME just opened a ticket, they're seeing 502s from service endpoints in eu-west-3 and failover to us-east is slow. Customer-facing impact: some API endpoints returning connection reset.

Devon L.: pulling dns logs from edge proxy. here's a quick grep:
```
2026-03-15T09:02:12Z edge-proxy-euw3b dns_query id=0x1a2 type=A name=acme-svc.privatelink.redwood.internal result=NXDOMAIN
2026-03-15T09:02:15Z edge-proxy-euw3b dns_query id=0x1a3 type=A name=acme-svc.privatelink.redwood.internal result=SERVFAIL
```

Mira K.: ok. Is this coming from our recursive resolvers or from the provider side? Run a dig +trace from a healthy node and one in AZ-b.

Jon P.: run from jump boxes:
```
# from euw3c (healthy)
$ dig +trace acme-svc.privatelink.redwood.internal
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1-Ubuntu <<>> +trace acme-svc.privatelink.redwood.internal
;; Received 192.0.2.53#53
acme-svc.privatelink.redwood.internal. 60 IN A 10.10.20.5

# from euw3b (failing)
$ dig +trace acme-svc.privatelink.redwood.internal
;; connection timed out; server 192.0.2.53#53 refused to respond
```

Priya S.: customer reports intermittent DNS for ~12 minutes, started 09:00 UTC. They've already tried restart on their side.

Mira K.: hypothesis: provider-side DNS rewrite/filtering in AZ-b or a misconfigured DNS proxy. Jon, can you check PrivateLink endpoint config and the iptables/DNSMasq on the host? Also check if Route 53 private hosted zone changed.

Jon P.: checking PrivateLink control plane now. No recent control-plane change in our audit logs for that endpoint. Control plane shows target ENIs in AZ-b healthy. Fetching host-level dnsmasq config and journal for 09:00-09:10.

Devon L.: found this in host journal for the PrivateLink NVA in euw3b:
```
Mar 15 09:01:58 nva-12 kernel: netfilter: DROP IN=eth0 OUT= MAC=.. SRC=198.51.100.23 DST=192.0.2.53 PROTO=UDP SPT=53 DPT=49123
Mar 15 09:02:04 nva-12 dnsmasq[2123]: suppressing PTR queries for private zone
```

Mira K.: interesting. Looks like some automated policy on the NVA is dropping DNS responses destined for our resolver. Any recent firewall rule changes from provider side or our config pushes?

Jon P.: checking config manager — no pushes to that cluster since yesterday. But I see a provider-managed firewall policy change at 08:59 UTC that aligns with the start of symptoms. Opening support with cloud provider: INC-20260315-8472.

ACME Ops Bot: Customer note — ACME reports 40% of requests failing, engineering on hold, escalation to their infra lead @acme-infra.

Priya S.: relaying to ACME: "We're investigating DNS anomalies affecting eu-west-3 AZ-b PrivateLink endpoint. We'll update in 15 mins." Customer acknowledged.

Mira K.: mitigation plan (short term): 1) divert PrivateLink traffic from AZ-b to AZ-c via routing policy. 2) add a temporary local resolver in AZ-b that bypasses the NVA. 3) escalate provider firewall rollback.

Devon L.: implementing route diversion. Command to add policy route:
```
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0abc123 --destination-cidr-block 10.10.20.0/24 --instance-id eni-id-euw3c
```
Applying now.

Jon P.: Adding a dnsmasq on NVA that points to 169.254.169.253 (local stub) and bypasses provider DNS. Config:
```
server=/privatelink.redwood.internal/169.254.169.253
listen-address=127.0.0.1
```
Deploying on euw3b NVA.

SRE-Bot: Handoff: Pager silence requested. On-call handoff at 09:30 UTC to Mira K. -> Jon P. remains as net lead.

Mira K.: diversion applied, confirmed traffic now takes AZ-c path. Customer telemetry shows error rate dropping to ~5%.

ACME Ops Bot: ACME: "seeing recovery on our side, thanks. We'll keep monitoring for 30m." :white_check_mark:

Priya S.: opening follow-up ticket to postmortem. Assigning to network-eng (Jon) and infra (Devon). PTR: PGT-20260315-ACME-01

Jon P.: provider acknowledged a misapplied firewall policy and started rollback. Will validate and then revert our temporary routes once stable.

Mira K.: final notes for incident record: root-cause preliminary = provider firewall policy applied to NVAs in eu-west-3 AZ-b causing DNS response drops. Impact = degraded PrivateLink DNS resolution for ACME, partial customer request failures. Mitigation = temporary route diversion to AZ-c + local stub resolver on NVA + provider rollback. Next steps = postmortem, confirm provider change freeze window, adjust detection to alert on resolver error spikes.

Devon L.: assigning oncall follow-up checklist: update runbook, add check for dnsmasq suppression logs, add guardian alert for >5% NXDOMAIN from internal resolvers.

Mira K.: closing thread — handing to postmortem owners. Thanks everyone. :pray:
